arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.

Original abstract

In this article we study the concept of product of two holomorphic correspondences which was introduced in our previous work. Beginning with some basic results regarding the orbit space associated with the product correspondence, we then move on to a detailed analysis on the thermodynamic formalism of the same. Some of the results look at the behaviour of the product correspondence with respect to the individual correspondences. Finally, we explore different families of correspondences with expanding nature.

arXiv:2611.01005 · new · high confidence

Positive expansiveness of operator semigroups: orbit growth and spectral criteria

Hien Minh Huynh

Relevance
Expansiveness and orbit growth are central topological-dynamics properties.
TL;DR
For strongly continuous linear-operator semigroups, the authors compare positive expansiveness, its kinematic version and uniform exponential expansion.
Problem
Characterize these expansion properties through orbit growth, the generator and spectral data.
Main result
Positive kinematic expansiveness is equivalent to unboundedness of every nonzero orbit; positive expansiveness additionally requires the generator to be bounded below. Uniform exponential expansion implies positive expansiveness without surjectivity and is characterized using minimum modulus, lower growth bound and approximate point spectrum of one semigroup operator. Under a uniform positive lower bound on the semigroup, the stated orbit-growth and generator conditions characterize positive expansiveness. Diagonal examples give a strict hierarchy of the three notions, which coincide in finite dimensions.

Context

Keywords

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

This paper studies positive expansiveness and positive kinematic expansiveness for strongly continuous semigroups of bounded linear operators on complex Banach spaces. We prove that positive kinematic expansiveness is equivalent to the unboundedness of every nonzero orbit, while positive expansiveness additionally requires the generator to be bounded from below. We also show that continuous changes of time can be replaced by increasing homeomorphisms without changing positive expansiveness. Uniform exponential expansion implies positive expansiveness without any surjectivity assumption; we characterize it through the minimum modulus, the lower growth bound, and the approximate point spectrum of a single semigroup operator. Under a uniform positive lower bound on the semigroup, positive expansiveness is equivalent to positive kinematic expansiveness together with boundedness below of the generator. Diagonal semigroups on then show that uniform exponential expansion, positive expansiveness and its kinematic version form a strictly decreasing hierarchy. Finally, we derive necessary spectral conditions for bounded generators and show that all three properties coincide in finite dimensions.

For a dissipation stochastic differential equation (abbreviated as SDE), exponential ergodicity has been investigated a lot in a wide range of settings. In this paper, we prove that the Markovian measure determined by the unique stationary measure is also the unique invariant measure which satisfies the entropy formula. Consequently, the existence of an SRB measure is completely determined by the sign of the sample top Lyapunov exponent of : if , then is the unique SRB measure, whereas if , then the SDE admits no SRB measure. As an application, we establish a dichotomy of SRB measures for the 2D additive-noise stochastic Hopf normal form within a shear parameter domain.

Original abstract

In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. Furthermore, we also construct a counterexample showing that the integrability condition above cannot in general be omitted.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We introduce two types of Bykov cycles for Filippov systems: crossing Bykov cycles, which retain the main dynamical features of their smooth counterparts, and sliding Bykov cycles, whose dynamics intrinsically involves the switching manifold. We construct explicit piecewise linear examples of both configurations. For crossing Bykov cycles, we prove the existence of hyperbolic invariant sets carrying symbolic dynamics, as in the classical smooth setting. For sliding Bykov cycles, under suitable open conditions, we obtain a countable symbolic dynamics on an invariant set; we prove that this invariant set has several interesting properties: the Hausdorff dimension of it and of its closure are equal, and it lies strictly between zero and one, and so both sets have zero Lebesgue measure; its closure is a Cantor set; and we also obtain conformal and invariant ergodic measures for the associated return dynamics. Finally, we show that convolution regularization of a suitable piecewise constant vector field produces a spatial cusp whose versal unfolding contains classical Bykov cycles. Thus, Bykov-type dynamics arises in the non-smooth setting both intrinsically, through crossing and sliding mechanisms, and through smooth regularization.

Original abstract

We study codimension one homoclinic flows on closed surfaces and introduce a complete topological invariant based on the structural graph of the flow and the distinguishing graphs of its atoms. This invariant completely determines the topological equivalence class of a homoclinic flow. For flows on the two-dimensional sphere, we construct a canonical coding algorithm that avoids the global renumbering required in the classical coding of Morse flows and substantially reduces the computational complexity. As an application, we derive recursive formulas for the number of topologically distinct homoclinic flows on the two-dimensional sphere and compute these numbers for flows with a small number of saddle singularities and closed orbits.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

The Hubbard-Wigner model describes binary lattice configurations with convex repulsive pair interactions. We give a unified classification of its periodic minimizers, minimizing invariant measures, and Aubry sets through a positive block-count identity, recovering explicit plateau widths and a complete devil's staircase for the minimizing density. This variational structure parallels Aubry-Mather theory and the authors' work on Aubry's completeness conjecture, where the staircase is related to the sliding and pinning mechanisms underlying the conducting and insulating interpretations of particle chains. In the binary model, completeness follows from discrete convexity and an exact sum of plateau widths. We then study how this classical structure persists for interactions arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect on a thin torus. At rational density , the diagonal reference has a -dimensional lowest eigenspace, a spectral gap uniform in the number of repeated periods, and an associated bundle of Chern number . For the full operator, we prove persistence of a density- plateau and a positive spectral gap, uniformly in system size at sufficiently small fixed transverse circumference; the lowest-eigenspace bundle has rank three and Chern number one. For the full periodic Coulomb operator, we establish multiplicity, spectral-gap, and Chern-number conclusions at bounded denominators, and quantitative bounds on plateau-endpoint displacement and loss of width under explicit joint conditions on size and geometry.

Original abstract

Let be a continuous self-map of a compact metric space. For each integer , we consider the upper capacity entropy scale obtained by dividing the -fold logarithm of an orbit covering number by the -fold logarithm of time. We prove that every nonempty compact set contains a compact subset realizing any value between zero and its own scale entropy. Every strictly intermediate value is realized by a countable compact set with exactly one accumulation point. The proof combines localization at a fixed spatial resolution, a finite-tree selection lemma, and refinements of orbit covers at dyadic times. An example shows that the assertion about one accumulation point does not extend to the upper endpoint. On the product-diagonal construction used in classical entropy lowerability, the diagonal scales preserve the values of the base subsets, although classical upper capacity entropy takes only zero or infinity.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

Viewing computing machines as symbolic dynamical systems is a powerful idea which has led to many important results. However, the standard setting of symbolic Turing dynamics is not well suited for studying questions of typicality, genericity, or robustness. Such natural questions, for example, as "what is the computational power of a typical computer program?", "how common is poly-time computability", or "how common is universal computation among all algorithms?" require a different approach. In this paper we develop a suitable general framework of viewing families of dynamical systems as computing devices. We study a specific class of such devices given by the logistic family, and give the answers to the above questions in this setting.

We develop a homological approach to the topological entropy of discontinuous interval maps with arbitrary branch orientations. Relations among the one-sided images of discontinuities reduce the kneading determinant, while symmetries yield further simplifications. We determine the smallest possible dimension of this reduction for each orientation pattern and show that this minimum can coexist with maximal entropy. The general theory is applied to maps with increasing or decreasing branches, extending earlier results for bimodal maps and yielding exact formulas for entropy and periodic-orbit counts.

Let be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let be an invariant Feller -algebra. We formulate the -property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Cesàro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the -property, the Jacobs–de Leeuw–Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi–Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner–Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Cesàro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Original abstract

The Lagrange spectrum is a classical object in number theory, defined as the set of values of where runs through irrational numbers. It has a complicated structure, with the discrete part, Hall's ray, and a transitional part in between. One can similarly define Lagrange spectrum in the multidimensional set-up, and until now not much has been understood about it. In this paper we prove that, unlike in the one-dimensional case, the closure of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum is equal to the interval between and its supremum. The proof relies on a correspondence between Diophantine approximation and dynamics on the space of unimodular lattices and proceeds by studying a dynamical counterpart of the Lagrange spectrum that we call dynamical Lagrange spectrum. The latter is shown to be equal to the interval between and its maximum by means of an argument utilizing the higher rank nature of the set-up. A passage from full dynamical spectrum to the density of the Diophantine spectrum is achieved by applying equidistribution of expanding translates of horospheres in the space of lattices.

The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.

When an unregularized trajectory reaches zero velocity in finite time, inner rescaling yields convergence to a reference orbit within the regularization ball, while the regularized trajectories converge locally uniformly outside it to a unique continuation. For the directional dynamics, stereographic projection yields a parameterized Euclidean system. By choosing the skew-symmetric magnetic part, we obtain a nonautonomous parameterized center manifold reduction with a prescribed finite Taylor jet. Under an additional factorization assumption, the reduced dynamics admits Shilnikov homoclinic orbits and associated chaos.

Original abstract

In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton–Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller–Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf–Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.

Original abstract

We study singularities of separation coordinates for geodesic flows of real-analytic two-dimensional (pseudo-)Riemannian metrics. We obtain a complete local classification of these singularities using the Nijenhuis operator associated with a quadratic first integral. The singular set is locally a smooth curve, an isolated point, or two transversely intersecting curves. We also show that orthogonal separation near one point of an analytic disk extends to a quadratic first integral on the entire disk and provide explicit separation coordinates near singularities.

Original abstract

Stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equations generally admit many weak KAM solutions. The question is how to select one weak KAM solution that reflects a meaningful physical principle. In this paper, we propose a selection principle for Hamilton-Jacobi equations arising from the large deviation principle of general drift-diffusion processes on based on the exponential asymptotics of invariant measures. We first characterize the Aubry set as the finitely many equilibria of the drift, using an action estimate from the orthogonal decomposition of the drift. For any boundary data on the Aubry set compatible with the Peierls barrier, we construct the unique coercive weak KAM solution with these boundary data, which is also the maximal locally Lipschitz viscosity solution. The Freidlin-Wentzell graph formula then provides the boundary data on the Aubry set that select the unique weak KAM solution. The selected solution is exactly the rate function in the large deviation principle for invariant measures in the zero noise limit. We also show that this rate function is the vanishing viscosity limit, to which the viscous approximations converge locally uniformly. Finally, under additional regularity assumptions, we show that the long-time and zero-noise limits commute for suitably prepared initial densities.

We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. Original abstract

We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. We apply the result in three settings: mixing for a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system where the scalar actively drives the velocity, mixing for a passive scalar advected by two-dimensional Navier-Stokes driven by smooth-in-time stochastic forcing, and a black-box proof that negative-regularity mixing implies enhanced dissipation.

Original abstract

The present work develops a Koopman–von Neumann (KvN) formulation of contact Hamiltonian dynamics on the Hilbert space defined by the contact volume. The resulting generator includes the divergence correction required for unitary evolution. We establish symmetry and, for complete contact Hamiltonian vector fields, essential self-adjointness and a strongly continuous unitary evolution; we also describe covariance under contactomorphisms. For completely integrable contact systems with complete flows, it is possible to recover an invariant direct-integral decomposition and strongly commuting KvN generators. We further relate contact KvN dynamics to the KvN formulation of its symplectization.
